signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Unwind
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 112.20 as a strong JPY outperformance theme dominates G10 flows. JPY 1W avg of +1.559% (n=7) vs CAD 1W avg of -0.909% (n=3) creates a massive 2.468% G10 spread, the widest bilateral divergence in the complex. This move is fundamentally supported by JPY’s Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.9, indicating sustained data beats that contrast sharply with CAD’s neutral +4.4. While CAD/JPY maintains a +125bp OIS carry advantage for CAD, the options market is aggressively pricing for further downside as USD/JPY 25d risk reversals hit -2.76, reflecting a significant put skew. The technical position for JPY is increasingly bullish, with USD/JPY now trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (161.88, 161.25, 158.00), suggesting a structural trend shift. Risk: Oil prices rebound above $85, providing idiosyncratic support to CAD and arresting the carry unwind.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Data + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1541 following a Eurozone Composite PMI beat to an eight-month high of 52.0. This macro strength supports the ECB's hike bias and narrows the real rate deficit vs the Fed, with the EUR real rate currently at +0.12% vs USD at +1.51%. Options markets show an elevated volatility risk premium (VRP) of +2.8, with IV at 7.1% vs HV30 at 4.3%, signaling that traders are paying up for EUR protection despite the spot pair trading above its SMA20/50 cluster (1.1438/1.1481). Speculative positioning remains a headwind as COT LF net short stands at -92,930 (long% 30.7%), but the ESI outperformance (+7.1) suggests a fundamental disconnect that favor bulls. A sustained hold above the 1.1481 SMA50 level targets the SMA200 at 1.1633. Risk: Fed Chair Warsh initiates structural FOMC reforms that aggressively re-price US terminal rates higher.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5865, underperforming its G10 peers (1W avg -0.446%) despite a hawkish RBNZ hike bias and a leading ESI of +24.4. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. This positioning reflects a crowded fade of the RBNZ's hawkishness, leaving the pair vulnerable to a significant short squeeze if the September 2 meeting delivers a hawkish surprise. The pair is technically healthy, holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5814/0.5793/0.5827), but retail sentiment (74% short) is currently aligned with the specs, reducing contrarian conviction for an immediate reversal. Risk: RBNZ pauses hiking cycle unexpectedly, validating the heavy speculative short position.

signals.title: GBP/USD — G10 Yield Support + Vol Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3460 remains supported by a neutral carry profile (Fed 3.75% vs BoE 3.75%) and the highest G10 10Y yield at 5.10%. The pair is trading above its entire SMA cluster (SMA20/50/200 at 1.3401, 1.3364, 1.3401), establishing 1.3400 as a major structural support floor. Options markets are pricing in significant tail risk with a VRP of +4.8 (IV 11.0% vs HV30 6.2%), indicating that despite the bullish price action, institutional desks are heavily hedged against downside moves. Speculative positioning is moderately long (lev_net +36,661, long% 67.3%), which suggests the trend is not yet at an exhaustion extreme. The next directional catalyst is the UK's ability to maintain its yield premium as US 10Y yields soften toward 4.62%. Risk: BoE shifts to a dovish bias at the September 17 meeting, erasing the yield advantage.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.538, significantly below its SMA200 (9.714) and all short-term moving averages. Retail sentiment has reached a total extreme with 99% of traders net long at Myfxbook, positioning for a USD/NOK rebound that continues to fail. This retail positioning directly diverges from the Norges Bank's restrictive stance, with a real policy rate of +1.51% (cb_rate 4.25% vs infl_exp 2.74%) supporting NOK strength. Brent oil prices holding near $76.2 provide a base for NOK despite recent 'deal hope' headlines pressuring the energy complex. Given the 99% retail long extreme, a further washout of retail longs toward the 9.40 level is the high-probability path if USD remains under pressure. Risk: Brent oil breaks below $70, triggering a sharp NOK sell-off and retail capitulation.
